description.value: The study used structural and functional MRI to investigate moral reasoning, default mode network recruitment, and directed network interactions in behavioural variant frontotemporal dementia and healthy control subjects.

spans.text: We aimed to reconcile the findings of activation-based and patient-based studies of the default mode network in personal moral reasoning by using functional MRI to study neural activity in patients with behavioural variant FTD and in normal control subjects during a moral reasoning task.

value: we hypothesized that the salience network plays a causal role in recruiting the default mode network during ‘personal’ moral dilemmas, and that abnormal moral judgement in behavioural variant FTD reflects a disruption of this causal influence.
